By the late nineteenth century, it is common to see only repeated sunburst medallions. description: We now enter the petroglyphs area of Gobustan- this is the real McCoy. The stone sign here is in Russian. The Gobustan Rock Art Cultural Landscape covers three areas of a plateau of rocky boulders rising out of the semi-desert of central Azerbaijan, with an outstanding collection of more than 6,000 rock engravings bearing testimony to 40,000 years of rock art. The site also features the remains of inhabited caves, settlements and burials, all reflecting an intensive human use by the inhabitants

terms: Creative Commons Zero, Public Domain Dedication
description: This image from an unfinished painting depicts one of the most popular episodes from the life of the pre-Islamic Persian king Bahram Gur (reigned AD 420–38). A famed hunter, he was challenged by his concubine, Azada, to strike a donkey through its foot and ear with a single arrow. Azada is in the upper right playing the harp on a camel. Bahram Gur successfully meets her challenge at the bottom of the page; he tossed a rock into the donkey's ear, then fired when the animal tried to kick it loose.
objectName: Bahram Gur and Azada, from a Shahnama (Book of Kings) of Firdausi (940-1019 or 1025)

description: This image from an unfinished painting depicts one of the most popular episodes from the life of the pre-Islamic Persian king Bahram Gur (reigned AD 420–38). A famed hunter, he was challenged by his concubine, Azada, to strike a donkey through its foot and ear with a single arrow. Azada is in the upper right playing the harp on a camel. Bahram Gur successfully meets her challenge at the bottom of the page; he tossed a rock into the donkey’s ear, then fired when the animal tried to kick it loose.

terms: Creative Commons Zero, Public Domain Dedication
description: Begun at the end of the reign of Shah Ismail (reigned 1501–24), first king of the Safavid dynasty of Iran, this copy of the Shah-nama (Book of Kings) was completed during the reign of his son Shah Tahmasp. Unparalleled in scope and refinement, the book included 259 paintings by master artists in the royal workshop. Two calligraphers copied the text in an elegant, flowing nasta‘liq script. In 1568, Shah Tahmasp gave this book as a gift to the Ottoman sultan Selim II of Turkey.

On the basis of the tightly wound turban with a thick bulge in front and a fanned end with flowers on a gold ground the painting can be dated to the 1690's or early eighteenth century. description: Shah Ismail confronted the Aq Qoyunlu leader Alwand (who was also ruler of Tabriz) before the Battle of Sharur (1501). He said, "We are both descendants of Uzun Hasan, who was the Ak Koyunlu Sultan; let's not fight." Ismail accepted this offer, suggesting that Alvand choose the Shia sect, in which case he would stop the war and pledge allegiance to Alvand. Alvand, however, did not accept and remained Sunni. objectName: Negotiations between Alwand and Ismail, followed by the battle of Sharur (1501). Habib al-siyar, end of 16th century. National Palace Museum (cropped)

title: File:Turkic emir Lord Muzaffar al-Dawla wal-Din in a battle at Khalkhāl. 1185-1210 CE (Freer Gallery of Art, F1943.3).jpg
credit: Free Gallery of Art Saracen Faris Ad 1050-1250, by Dr David Nicolle, Osprey Publishing, 1994, ISBN-13:978-1855324534 Holod, Renata, "Event and Memory: The Freer Gallery's Siege Scene Plate", Ars Orien
description: Depiction of Turkic emir "Lord Muzaffar al-Dawla wal-Din" (inscription around the figure, "Lord Muzaffar al-Dawla wal-Din", خداوند مظفر الدوله و الدين), "a member of the Turkish military emir class" at a siege in Khalkhal . Painted circa 1200 (likely 1185-1210). Most likely: near-contemporary depiction of Muzaffar al-Dīn Qizil Arslān (Eldegüzid ruler 1186-1191) besieging Khalkhal . Alternatively (and less likely): Muzaffar al-Dīn Abù Bakr (Salghurid ruler 1226-1260), in alliance with the Khwariz
objectName: Turkic emir Lord Muzaffar al-Dawla wal-Din in a battle at Khalkhāl. 1185-1210 CE (Freer Gallery of Art, F1943.3)

description: One-ruble ticket for the fifth All-Union Osoaviakhim lottery, series 021057, no. 098, division X. The society’s emblem, the Soviet coat of arms and a motto about peaceful labour and Soviet defence run across the top. Aeroplanes, an airship labelled Osoaviakhim, a wheeled tractor with its driver and a tank appear against industrial buildings, framed by chains and hooks. Below are a call to strengthen Soviet defence and the ticket title in languages of the Soviet republics. Reddish-brown printing

description: נשיא המדינה יצחק הרצוג ו רעייתו מיכל , נחתו בבאקו, אזרבייג'ן לביקורם הממלכתי. עם נחיתתם, התקבלו הנשיא ורעייתו בשדה התעופה במשמר כבוד על ידי נציגים מהצד האזרי ו-30 ילדים מביה״ס היהודי חב״ד (אור אבנר) שבבאקו בשירת ״הבאנו שלום עליכם״. את פניהם קיבלו סגן ראש ממשלת אזרבייג'ן, יגוב איובוב, סגן שר החוץ של אזרבייג'ן, פריז רזאייב, שגריר אזרבייג'ן בישראל, מוכתר ממד אוגלו ממדוב ושגריר מדינת ישראל באזרבייג'ן, ג'ורג' דיק. יום שלישי, י' בסיון תשפ"ג, 30 במאי 2023. קרדיט צילום: חיים צח/לע"ם.

description: נשיא המדינה יצחק הרצוג ו רעייתו מיכל , נחתו בבאקו, אזרבייג'ן לביקורם הממלכתי. עם נחיתתם, התקבלו הנשיא ורעייתו בשדה התעופה במשמר כבוד על ידי נציגים מהצד האזרי ו-30 ילדים מביה״ס היהודי חב״ד (אור אבנר) שבבאקו בשירת ״הבאנו שלום עליכם״. את פניהם קיבלו סגן ראש ממשלת אזרבייג'ן, יגוב איובוב, סגן שר החוץ של אזרבייג'ן, פריז רזאייב, שגריר אזרבייג'ן בישראל, מוכתר ממד אוגלו ממדוב ושגריר מדינת ישראל באזרבייג'ן, ג'ורג' דיק. יום שלישי, י' בסיון תשפ"ג, 30 במאי 2023. קרדיט צילום: חיים צח/לע"ם.
objectName: Isaac Herzog state visit to Azerbaijan
cats: Isaac Herzog state visit to Azerbaijan

title: File:Nude Woman In Marble by sculptor Ahmet Tsalikov.jpg

title: File:Old Azerbaijan Lady by sculptor Ahmet Tsalikov.jpg

objectName: Old Azerbaijan Lady by sculptor Ahmet Tsalikov

title: File:Uzeir Gadjibekov in Marble by Ahmet Tsalikov.jpg
description: Бюст Узеира Гаджибекова (1885-1948), советского и азербайджанского композитора, родившегося близ города Шуша (Нагорный Карабах). Ахмет Цаликов также являлся автором монументу композитору установленному на родине Гаджибекова в 80-е годы XX века. Бюст хранится в мастерской художника, а фотография предоставлена из личного архива Ахмета Бацкоевича Цаликова

title: File:Byurakan-min-63cf.jpg

На почтовой марке карточки изображено здание главного и самого большого телескопа Бюраканской астрофизической обсерватории имени В. Амбарцумяна на фоне вселенной. title: File:Bozbash from Iranian (Azeri) cuisine.jpg
description: "Bozbaş" or "Bozbash" from Iranian (Azeri) cuisine. (Some Azeris in Turkey, for example in Iğdır, and elsewhere (parts of Iran and Azerbaijan) call " piti " as "bozbaş". (Whereas in Kars it is "piti".) I ate this dish at an Iranian Azeri restaurant in Ankara. It is very similar to the "piti" or "bozbaş" we have in Turkey and Azerbaijan but I noticed that, other than chickpeas, they use dried white beans and they do not use the herb (what we call "sarıkök") that gives the dish its greenish yellow

description: While Afrasiyab fights at Dahistan, a supplementary force is detailed to attack Zabul, home of Zal, of which Mihrab has been left in charge. Through bribery and persuasion, he keeps the Turanians at bay. An urgent message reaches Zal, who returns immediately with his army. He soon dispatches Khazarvan, one of the Turanian commanders, by smashing him on the head with his ox-head mace, then trampling him to death; Painting attributed to 'Abd al-Vahhab

terms: Creative Commons Zero, Public Domain Dedication
description: Single polychrome paintings of elegantly clad youth were produced in considerable number during the 1600s, primarily for people with means who collected them and had them mounted in albums. Instead of functioning as portraits, the images of these courtly figures express ideals of youth and beauty. This young man's lavish sash and turban enriched with costly gold thread proclaim his high status.

title: File:A manuscript of the Gulistan (Rosegarden) by Sa’di; Sa’di in a Rose garden (FGA F1998.5).jpg
description: A manuscript of the Gulistan (Rosegarden) by Sa’di; Sa’di in a Rose garden. It was copied in 1468 by the Sultan Ali Mashhadi in Herat. Sometime during the early sixteenth century, the margins of its first sixteen folios were lavishly illuminated. The exquisite design, consisting of arabesques with mythical and real animals in fierce combat or intricate floral motifs, have been attributed to Aqa Mirak, one of the leading artists of the court of Shah Tahmasb (reigned 1524-76). title: File:Mohammed kaaba 1315 bew.jpg
credit: Jami' al-Tavarikh ("The Compendium of Chronicles" or "The Universal History") This illustration is in a folio in the Oriental Manuscript Section of the Edinburgh University Library, Special Collection
description: Prophet Muhammad solves a dispute over lifting the black stone into position at al-Kaaba. Note from pp. 100-101 of "The illustrations to the World history of Rashid al-Din / David Talbot Rice ; edited by Basil Gray. Edinburgh : Edinburgh University Press, c1976." - In the center, Prophet Muhammad, with two long hair plaits, places the stone on a carpet held at the four corners by representatives of the four tribes, so that all have the honor of lifting it. The carpet is a kelim from Central Asia
cats: Muhammad helping in placing the Black Stone
